decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Recent indicators have been mixed and the adjustment in the housing sector is ongoing.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to acknowledge that recent data is mixed and housing adjustments continue.

changes.quote: Recent readings on core inflation have been somewhat elevated.
changes.explanation: This new sentence highlights that core inflation readings have stayed somewhat elevated.

changes.quote: In these circumstances, the Committee's predominant policy concern remains the risk that inflation will fail to moderate as expected.
changes.explanation: This added text explicitly notes that inflation remaining high is the primary concern for policy.

changes.quote: Future policy adjustments will depend on the evolution of the outlook for both inflation and economic growth, as implied by incoming information.
changes.explanation: The Fed changed its forward-looking sentence to focus on incoming information for any future policy adjustments.

tone_quotes.quote: Recent readings on core inflation have been somewhat elevated.
In these circumstances, the Committee's predominant policy concern remains the risk that inflation will fail to moderate as expected.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.31% APR costs about $55.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.53% and moved -3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.14% would fall by about $5.82 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.5%, and employers added an average of 167k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.4% over the past year (February 2007); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -9 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.18% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future policy decisions will depend entirely on incoming data regarding inflation and economic growth.
